newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla mulls changes, course not known.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla mulls changes, course not known.

text.p: Odwalla Inc founder and chairman Greg Steltenpohl said on Monday the fruit juice producer "is considering pasteurization" as a way to prevent future outbreaks of E-coli in its products, but that it was too early to tell if that is the right course.

"We think it's too early to state as to exactly what processes will change inside of our production plant regarding the production of apple juice," he told a press conference in Denver, where a number of cases of E-coli have been linked to Odwalla's products.
Steltenpohl was asked a number of times by reporters if pasteurization was the proper route, but each time said it was too early to determine new policies until further scientific study is conducted.
Federal officials have confirmed 29 cases of bacterial poisoning linked to fresh apple juice and the Center for Disease Control is expected to issue an update later Monday, Steltenpohl said.
He said the company has been "moved by the degree of consumer support" it has received.
